sense.text:
“Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” So we lack truth, we lack mercy, and we lack knowledge of the Lord in the land. That is our issue.

And that is what we see in today's society, and not only among the youth, because some of the adults are off as well: adults with grey hairs and beards doing some dumb stuff out there. But the youth are a generation we need to get a hold of, because it is not good how some of them are moving. Not all, but some are moving really bad.

No truth, no knowledge of God in the land. No mercy in the land.

“By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood”. These are the issues within our community, and one of them is blood toucheth blood.

When you research what blood toucheth blood means, it goes into a continuous uninterrupted violence. Continuous, uninterrupted violence. And that is what a lot of our people specialize in.

It is not just today that we are seeing it. We can go back into the scriptures and see that we moved that way: we had that spirit on us from the earlier days, from the earlier days of the kings of Israel.

“In the thirty and eighth year of Azariah king of Judah did Zachariah the son of Jeroboam reign over Israel in Samaria six months.” Zachariah the son of Jeroboam, reigning over Israel — the northern kingdom, in Samaria — six months. Six months.

We are going to show you how wicked our people were back then, and how lustful for power we were.

“And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his fathers had done: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.” So he did what we do best, which is evil, as his fathers had done.

Our forefathers, our kings — and here we are dealing with the northern kingdom — made us to sin. They made us to sin. They did evil in the sight of the Lord and they made us to sin.

“And Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.” So he killed him in front of the people and reigned in his stead. That was a public assassination: public execution, public murder, whichever word you want to put on it. He did it publicly and took over the kingship.

Read verse 8 and it says six months he was in power; then he was killed by Shallum, killed publicly, and Shallum reigned in his stead.

So the stabbing in the chicken shop on Brixton Road that was shown at the start is nothing new under the sun, because that was a public attempted execution, a public attempted assassination if you want to call it that. The mindset was the same back then among our people.

precepts.why:
“Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.” But read on: “Howbeit from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, Jehu departed not from after them, to wit, the golden calves that were in Beth–el, and that were in Dan.” So although he destroyed Baal out of Israel, there were still sins he committed. He departed not from the golden calves which are in Beth-el and that were in Dan. He still kept them.

Then the word to Jehu: “And the Lord said unto Jehu, Because thou hast done well in executing that which is right in mine eyes, and hast done unto the house of Ahab according to all that was in mine heart, thy children of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.” Take the chart of the kings and count the fourth generation from Jehu — Jehoahaz, Joash, Jeroboam the second, and Zachariah, the one we are reading about. That was the end of it, the end of the fourth generation. Then Shallum came and executed him. Zachariah reigned six months, and Shallum only reigned one month.

So that prophecy came to pass to this fourth generation. That is one example of blood toucheth blood; now we are going to see another.

sense.text:
“Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the nine and thirtieth year of Uzziah king of Judah; and he reigned a full month in Samaria.” A full month. One month, thirty days — the same as you see it on the chart of the kings.

And when you read about Judah, Judah was on point. The northern kingdom were going off. Some are going to be mad at that, but it is what it is.

“For Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, and came to Samaria, and smote Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.” He travelled from Tirzah and came to Samaria and smote Shallum. So he killed him: another assassination. He slew him and reigned in his stead.

We are reading about how evil our people were, that lust for power. They were killing each other. Being a king did not guarantee your life; in fact your life was marked at that time. That is how our people moved.

It goes back to what we read in Hosea 4 and verse 2 about the continuous uninterrupted violence. That is why Hosea was getting on our people; that is what he was prophesying about.

“And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he made, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.” When you analyse just this time period — you read about Zachariah, then you read about Shallum — you can see the instability that was within our community at that time. We were a very unstable nation, because six months you have a king, then one month you have a king. You can imagine the chaos that was within that society.

And the same things have happened in this time. Colombia: a president murdered in 1984, and two years later another one assassinated — Rodrigo Lara Bonilla. That was the time of a lot of the drug trafficking going into the States, a lot of the coke that was taken from the coca plants in Colombia going over there. Israel has always been in wickedness.

That is why we need these commandments, so that we can get back. The split, idolatry, sin, all of that happened, and then the two kings separated. But it is showing you that the same things happen today. Blood toucheth blood. It is a power struggle; everyone is trying to outdo their brother, and that is exactly the same thing happening today.

“Then Menahem smote Tiphsah, and all that were therein, and the coasts thereof from Tirzah: because they opened not to him, therefore he smote it; and all the women therein that were with child he ripped up.” They opened not to him. Like we mentioned a minute ago, there was political and social instability in the community, so the people did not know who their king was. They were confused, and they decided, we are not going to open to him. Remember a lot of them would have had an allegiance to Shallum: you have come and taken him out, and now you want us to have you as king? They said no, so his answer was to smite them.

That is how evil he was. You talk about hatred — hatred to your own people — and this is a prime example right here. He killed the people, and the women that had children in them he ripped up. How much more evil can you get than that? Blood toucheth blood. Continual violence. Continual violence. That is what our communities had to go through at the time.

These nations' rise to power coincides with our demise, and we sank lower than the nations around us at the time. And the same way today, in some ways we have done the same in how we deal with each other. Crime happens in every society, but we are good at what we do towards each other; the evil we do against each other, we sometimes specialize in that. It is horrible to see.

That is why the Lord had to charge us. He had to bring a lawsuit against our nation for what we did, for how we are dealing with each other.

“In the nine and thirtieth year of Azariah king of Judah began Menahem the son of Gadi to reign over Israel, and reigned ten years in Samaria.” He reigned ten years in Samaria, the same way it says it on the chart. Ten years. He had a ten-year stint of evil towards our people.

precepts.why:
When you look at the history of what Menahem did, it was normally the Assyrians that did that. They had a history of doing that to our women, or to women in general: ripping babies out of their bellies, out of the stomachs.

Hazael was appointed king of Syria, and it is written: “And Hazael said, Why weepeth my lord? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child.” That is what they did. Slay with the sword, dash their children, and rip up their women with child. That was their trademark.

And that is what our forefathers adopted towards our own people. How evil we were: we were worse than the damn heathen. Worse than the heathen.

“Samaria shall become desolate; for she hath rebelled against her God: they shall fall by the sword: their infants shall be dashed in pieces, and their women with child shall be ripped up.” This is going into Syria invading Israel.

The prophecy: Samaria shall become desolate, for she hath rebelled against her God — idolatry. They shall fall by the sword, their infants shall be dashed in pieces, and their women with child shall be ripped up. There you go. So that is how they move towards us.

Then go back to 2 Kings 15 and verse 16 and read it again: Menahem smote Tiphsah, and all the women therein that were with child he ripped up. Their goal was to wipe out our generations; that is what they wanted to do. You read about it in the book of Matthew as well, during the time of Christ, and you can go back to Egypt as well. These nations have always wanted to wipe us out as a generation.

sense.text: “In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah Pekahiah the son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned two years.” There you go, Pekahiah. He began to reign over Israel in Samaria and reigned two years — two years, the same as you see it there on the chart.
“And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.” Surprise, surprise. Evil again.

“But Pekah the son of Remaliah, a captain of his, conspired against him, and smote him in Samaria, in the palace of the king’s house, with Argob and Arieh, and with him fifty men of the Gileadites: and he killed him, and reigned in his room.” So what happened? His own captain, the captain of his own host, conspired against him, killed him, and reigned in his room. So your own people did this to you.

You see, the trend continues, and continues, and continues. That is how we moved back then: we had a history of killing each other, that lust for power — political power, military power, whatever you want to call it — that desire to shed blood. And all this time the people are just confused, seeing king after king get killed and assassinated, taken out, whichever word you want to use.

What that shows is that the oaths of allegiance meant nothing. Meant nothing. You say you have an oath of allegiance to your brother, an oath of allegiance to whoever is around you — that brotherhood meant absolutely zero.

“In the two and fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned twenty years.” So after Pekah took out Pekahiah, he began to reign in Samaria, and he reigned twenty years, as you can see on the chart. Twenty years he reigned.
“And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.” Surprise, surprise. Evil again.

“In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath–pileser king of Assyria, and took Ijon, and Abel–beth–maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.” So now the Lord's prophecy is coming to pass. The king of Assyria came.

Now we are starting to go into slavery, into the Assyrian captivity. Now you are seeing it take place, we are reading about it, and all of this is under the rulership of Pekah, king of Israel.

“And Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and smote him, and slew him, and reigned in his stead, in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.” So now we are reading about Hoshea conspiring against Pekah. And he smote him. And he slew him. So the trend continues. It is continuing, that blood toucheth blood, continuous uninterrupted violence. That is what they were going through at the time.

Hoshea was the last king before the Assyrian captivity. When you jump two chapters onwards, to chapter 17, you read more about the Assyrian captivity there. But you can see the trend of how our forefathers, the kings, were towards one another, that lust for power.

And that is how you know that whatever has been happening, the same spirits are doing the same thing today. What we see today with the violence in our communities was happening back then, and there are many more examples besides.

“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” The things we are reading about here, the same things we read about our forefathers doing, these are the things that shall be — meaning the same spirits are back doing the same thing.

So now our job is to wake up the twelve tribes. That is your job. Let them know: listen, keep God's commandments. Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart. You should let them know that, because guess what — we have a trend of doing it. Our kings, our leaders were doing it.

You read the same thing happening in the continent of Africa, the same thing. The Israelites that are scattered out there, the same thing: power struggle, assassination upon assassination. The captain in Burkina Faso, they are trying to use his own people against him, and they say there have been dozens of attempts on his life; his closest man was offered five million to take him out. They always try to use their own people to assassinate — you read about Sankara. And the average negro would take that money: five million, that could change my life, and you are already seeing yourself on the beach in the Bahamas. Our people are bugged out.

There is no new thing. It is the same spirits today. That is why the prophets are back again teaching Israel: thus saith the Lord, keep my commandments and live. Then we will not have to be burying one another like this. A lot of us are burying our brethren.

precepts.why:
It goes into what we read in Ecclesiastes 1 and 9: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

That is why we need to study. That is why we need to be able to read the scriptures, go into the history and understand that those spirits there are the same spirits we are going to deal with today. Those issues there are the same issues we are going to deal with today. The killings that were happening among our people back then, that lust for power, that lust for political power, for money — all these spirits that were out there, they exist now.

It is not different. Oh, we are in 2020, whatever year, we are good; those are old times, those are the olden days, Bible days. No — it is the same today as it was back then.

sense.text:
“Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away.” This is what the Lord says the repercussions are of how we deal with each other. The land is going to mourn because of the killings and these other spirits, these hatred spirits, pre-eminence and all these evil spirits we have towards each other. The land mourns.

And every one that dwelleth therein shall languish. That is why we languish. Our spirits are off now, we are lost, we are languishing, we do not know who we are. You just languish; you walk around blind.

precepts.why:
“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger.” That is where the Lord says, I am going to take your heritage from you.

That is the lawsuit the Lord took out against us. He took out a lawsuit against the nation because of our evil, and these are the repercussions: you serve your enemies, you forget who you are, you are going to languish.

So when Hosea says every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, this is what the languishing is: discontinued from your own heritage and serving your enemies in a land you do not even know.

sense.text:
It goes back to Genesis. When our blood is shed, our blood cries to the Lord. “And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.”

That is what we need to understand. When we do wickedness, when we go around killing each other, our blood cries to the Lord. It cries to the Lord. The Lord does not fail to hear it or see it.

All the killings and the assassinations we read about in 2 Kings 15 did not go unnoticed. So when our brothers and sisters are going around killing, it is not going unchecked or unnoticed by the Lord.

precepts.why:
It says the same thing: “So ye shall not pollute the land wherein ye are: for blood it defileth the land: and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it.”

So this bloodshed defiles the land. It defiles the land. And the land cannot be cleansed of the blood that is shed therein.

So you have got to be careful when you are out trying to plot against your brother or your sister. Listen, that cannot be cleansed — but by the blood of him that shed it.

sense.text:
Another example of the wickedness, Bible days: “And Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem unto his mother’s brethren, and communed with them, and with all the family of the house of his mother’s father, saying,”

So you are reading about a brother who had a lust for power. He wanted power. He wanted to rule.

“Speak, I pray you, in the ears of all the men of Shechem, Whether is better for you, either that all the sons of Jerubbaal, which are threescore and ten persons, reign over you, or that one reign over you? remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.” Threescore and ten persons is seventy — a score is twenty, so twenty, twenty, twenty and ten: seventy men to rule over you.

So decide: do you want seventy of the brothers to reign over you, or do you just want me to reign over you? And remember, I am your bone and your flesh.

“And his mother’s brethren spake of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem all these words: and their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech; for they said, He is our brother.” So they decided to follow him because he is our brother. Simple as hell. But anyway, they did.

“And they gave him threescore and ten pieces of silver out of the house of Baal–berith, wherewith Abimelech hired vain and light persons, which followed him.” And that is what you see with people who have that lust — if it is power, money, pre-eminence, position, that lust to kill, to harm: they always pick dumb people to put around them. Light people, people that cannot think, that have damn wood between their head.

Because when it comes on — whatever country it is, UK's or America's dumbest criminals — you just sit back watching and you think, how can this person be so dumb? You have just got yourself locked up for life for the most dumbest of things. Stop being a damn fool.

But that is how it works. You do not want anyone intelligent around you, because they are going to pick up on your BS and you have got a bigger problem. So you want to pick yes men, yes women around you, that just do what you want; whatever you ask them to do, they will do it. So he was smart, he knew this, and he said, let me pick the dumbest of the dumb men to be around me.

“And he went unto his father’s house at Ophrah, and slew his brethren the sons of Jerubbaal, being threescore and ten persons, upon one stone: notwithstanding yet Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left; for he hid himself.” To kill seventy of your brothers — you know how evil you must be? How lustful for power must you be, or how off must you be, to do that? But this is what we are reading here.

Nothing new under the sun, so that same spirit we are reading about here is going to exist today.

And one was left, and he hid himself. So the Lord preserved one of them for a purpose.

“When Abimelech had reigned three years over Israel, Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem; and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech:” He had three years, three years over Israel. And what happened? The Lord sent an evil spirit between them.

Abimelech made an allegiance with the men of Shechem. They loved each other: best of buddies, best friends, brothers, you name it — for a season. They are designed for a season. Brothers in evil and wickedness for a season. See how the Lord flipped the switch, flipped the script.

That is why we warn you: choose your friends carefully. You choose your friends in wickedness and you think you have an allegiance — be mindful the Lord does not send an evil spirit between you. When you are aligned in evil, you pair up with someone, you are talking evil with each other, you are best friends now, you have your little conversations about so-and-so, about brothers, sisters, leadership, and everything is good between you — you are marking yourself. You are marking yourself, because the Lord will flip the switch and it will have you at each other's throats down the line. Your little gossip buddies, the ones you think are your best friends right now in evil: see how it is a couple of years down the line. It may not even last a couple of years.

We warn you. Prove your friends wisely and pick righteous friends. Pick righteous friends.

“That the cruelty done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, which slew them; and upon the men of Shechem, which aided him in the killing of his brethren.” The blood cried to the Lord, and the Lord said, you know what, I am going to flip the switch back on Abimelech. That is what he did.

And upon the men of Shechem which aided him in the killing of his brethren. You are a co-conspirator. Co-conspirator. You are associated — guilty by association and action. It says here, aided him in the killing of his brethren. So the Lord flipped the switch and he put the blood back on them.

“And the men of Shechem set liers in wait for him in the top of the mountains, and they robbed all that came along that way by them: and it was told Abimelech.” See how the Lord flipped it. Now, from being on one accord, they are laying in wait for him.

precepts.why:
“Of whom is Hymeneus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.” So the Lord delivers people to the devil.

That is what we have just read in Judges 9: the Lord sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and it ended with their blood laid back on them. The Lord can mark you and deliver you to Satan.

So that spirit, you need to keep in check. If you have got that murderous spirit on you, you need to check that spirit. You need to definitely check that spirit.

sense.text:
“The good man is perished out of the earth: and there is none upright among men: they all lie in wait for blood; they hunt every man his brother with a net.” That is the spirit that is in our community. We read it in 2 Kings 15, and there are many other scriptures besides, but it applies today: they all lie in wait for blood, they hunt every man his brother with a net.

The teens who danced and celebrated after stabbing and shooting a man at Hackney Central Station — the twenty-year-old victim shot and stabbed multiple times in broad daylight, a video of the group dancing found on one of the teens' phones which helped convict the group, and they were jailed for a total of seventy-seven years between them. This is you. You wait for blood, you kill, and you celebrate killing.

One, it is wrong what they did. But two — remember we read about Abimelech picking vain and light men to do his will with him; it is the same here. You have to be stupid: one, to do the crime, and two, to do a TikTok, or whatever social media platform it is, or record it on your phone and have it out there. You have to be pretty slow. Seventy-seven years between them, and that is good; it should have got life.

“That they may do evil with both hands earnestly, the prince asketh, and the judge asketh for a reward; and the great man, he uttereth his mischievous desire: so they wrap it up.” We do evil with both hands earnestly. That is what we do as a people. We do evil with both our hands earnestly. And the prince and the judge ask for a reward, and the great man utters his mischievous desire: so they wrap it up.

Look at this foolishness: men fighting in public with blades, a long machete. Look at the negroes. What the hell are they doing? What do you think they are fighting over? What is so important that they have to fight like that in public with knives? One of them ended up on his own backside. But that is the state of our people.

So we are predators towards each other. We are predators. We hunt each other. We are predatory towards each other, and we are always trying to ambush each other. That is how we are.

“Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom.” So be careful of your friends. Prove your friends carefully, from youth, because foolishness starts from young. It starts from young.

The video of school children doing some stupidness: this is why you have got to teach your children to prove their friends carefully, because this could easily turn into a death. Someone pulls out a knife, puts it in the wrong place, and now we are dealing with a fatality. And these are young children.

This is the UK. This is how it moves in the UK, and that is just a snippet of what goes down out here. We do not have guns like that here, but we specialize in knives out here. We are butchers out here. Trust me, we are butchers out here, because we do not have guns like that. We do, do not get me wrong, but knives are ninety per cent of what people carry as a weapon out here.

“Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up.” And that is what we need to do as a people. We need to return to our God, because he has smitten us. He has torn and he will heal us; he has smitten and he will bind us up.

When you analyse what has happened to us as a people over the years, our punishment has been a harsh punishment. From when the Lord said he would send our enemies against us, from when they landed where we were till today, the atrocities that have happened — this is just a snippet. A snippet.

“Therefore have I hewed them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth: and thy judgments are as the light that goeth forth.” So the Lord has used prophets to always warn us and tell us: listen, do not do this, do not do that, but do this and do that. The prophets have always warned our people what we should do.

So it says, I have slain them by the words of my mouth.

“For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.” So the Lord desired mercy. And the Lord has been merciful to us, because he could have wiped us out as a nation if he wanted to. He has had every right to wipe us out as a nation. But he desired mercy. The same thing Hosea 4 says we lack: we lack mercy towards one another.

And the videos show that we have no mercy. There are millions of these type of videos out there on social media platforms of how we deal with one another. The CCTV of the knife attack: the brother on the bike is just doing his job, he delivers food, and the man wants his bike. You laugh, but that is the guy's livelihood. He feeds his family from that. He loses that bike, what has he got left to feed his family? He knows that is his livelihood, he needs his bike, he has got to fight for it — most people would not, and the man has got a knife on him. Just see how we lack mercy in all walks of life. Our people are gone. The Lord says, I desired mercy, but when you behave like this I have to bring that lawsuit against you people.

It was never about sacrifice. He just wanted us to deal right by one another. Deal right with each other: mercy, not sacrifice. And keep the commandments, rather than you bringing animals to burn.
“But they like men have transgressed the covenant: there have they dealt treacherously against me.” We broke the covenant. Hence the lawsuit the Lord brought against us as a nation.

“And as troops of robbers wait for a man, so the company of priests murder in the way by consent: for they commit lewdness.” Verse 9 is going back into the history. In the margin of a 1611, next to verse 9, it reads: or, cunning for blood; Hebrew, with one shoulder; or, to Shechem. With one shoulder — so they were on one accord — and it mentions that word, Shechem.

The priests were on one accord to murder. Remember people going to Shechem, one of the cities of refuge, to seek refuge. But the priests knew, okay, there is this route they were going; we can rob people, we can rob them on the way. For they commit lewdness.

This is a criminal enterprise we are reading about right here. You may think it is the olden days, they are wearing sandals and it was all good. No, this was organized crime. They were robbing people, taking their goods, obviously money, their animals, anything they travelled with; they were organized to rob them for it. So the company of priests murder in the way by consent. It shows how evil our people are from top down.

“I have seen an horrible thing in the house of Israel: there is the whoredom of Ephraim, Israel is defiled.” That is why the Lord had to say that he has seen a horrible thing. So just imagine how the Lord feels about us today when he sees the foolishness we do: these videos, all the way we behave in society today. It is a horrible thing for the Lord to see.

There is the whoredom of Ephraim, and Israel is defiled. We are a defiled people.

“Also, O Judah, he hath set an harvest for thee, when I returned the captivity of my people.” Judah today is evil as hell. So it is not just Ephraim. We are all evil. We are all off in many different ways.

So that is an example again of blood toucheth blood. It has always been the case that we have been evil towards each other. We have had an evil eye. We deal with each other in a nasty way, from back then all the way to now. Nothing has changed.

precepts.why:
When you read the history of what Shechem means in Joshua 20, there were six places of refuge the Lord gave us: “And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment, and until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days: then shall the slayer return, and come unto his own city, and unto his own house, unto the city from whence he fled.” These are places of refuge where people could go and hide or stay without fear.

Then the cities themselves: “And they appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, and Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath–arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah.” There you go. Shechem. There is that word, in mount Ephraim. These are the six cities of refuge.

So go back to Hosea 6 and read verse 9 again, and you read what the priests did and how wicked we were. People were travelling to a city of refuge for their lives, and the company of priests knew the road and waited on it to rob and to murder.

sense.text: “For the ungodly and his ungodliness are both alike hateful unto God.” So the Lord does not like it when we deal treacherously with each other, when we hate and shed blood. He hates that. He does not like it. Make it clear to you: he does not like it.

“Therefore even upon the idols of the Gentiles shall there be a visitation: because in the creature of God they are become an abomination, and stumblingblocks to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the unwise.” There is going to be a visitation upon the idols of the Gentiles. Because a lot of these idols out there that Esau has put out there have become a stumbling block to our people. They have become a stumbling block to our people. Our people are bugged out and confused.

And a snare to the feet of the unwise. Because if you are in wisdom, you are going to be wise — there is a whole book of wisdom, which is what we are reading here. If you have the wisdom you are going to be able to spot what is right and what is wrong; for the most part, because people still make mistakes. Whereas if you have no wisdom you are easily taken. Easily taken.

You damn watch a video of a man wearing freaking what women wear — skirts, dresses and all that stuff. Now you are following a trend: I look cute in the skirt, because you have no wisdom to understand that you are not meant to wear what women wear. She wears high heels, I want to wear high heels as a man. There is no wisdom in that. You are carried away with that ideological mindset.

“For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication.” The devising — the thought and the creation — of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication. And this goes into Adam and Eve. That was the beginning of the spiritual fornication, the idolatry spirit that they had. It was idolatry. Idolatry. It is the beginning of spiritual fornication.

And these are the idols we follow today. Buddha, Mary, Krishna, money, all these fake religions — all idolatry, idols, idols, idols we follow today. But remember it says, a snare to the feet of the unwise. All these people you read there, they are not wise. They have no wisdom of the scriptures, so they will follow them.

Then fast forward to today, to the idols we follow today. It goes into your phones. Is your phone an idol? Some people lose their phone and they are ready to kill someone. Think about it: if you did not have your phone, ask yourself what extremes you would go to, what lengths you would go to, either to get it back or to get a new one immediately. Some people have a panic attack if they lose their phone; some would need oxygen, because they depend so much on their phone. It is that much of an idol. You would be rocking back and forth going cold turkey. You would think life does not exist any more: how would I survive, how do I get through the day? Your little Facebook, your little Twitter, your Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat — you do not have it and you feel lost, you feel like your life becomes of no value.

Sports is an idol. No one is saying you cannot play sports to keep healthy; it is a good way to keep fit, a good way to stay in the green. But for some it becomes an idol, where it takes over your life. You do not want to keep the Sabbath because there is a sports event on today. The World Cup. You do not want to keep the Sabbath because of the World Cup or the Super Bowl: I cannot keep the Sabbath, I cannot go to camp, I cannot go to the fly mission, because I have to watch the Super Bowl game, or the basketball, the NBA game.

Money is an idol. People do anything for money, for the most part. Your dream job becomes an idol. Food becomes an idol: you become a glutton and you need a fix of whatever it is. You have a mad craving for sugar — sugar is an idol, believe it or not; we are addicted to sugar. You drive three hours to get the cake you want, because your supermarket or store does not have it in stock, and you check to see if they have got it, because you fiend for it. Same way as drugs: if the dealer is three hours away and he is the only one in the area, you drive three hours to get your crack fix, or your weed, whichever one it is. Then clothes. And women can be an idol — and you men do not go quiet, because some of you are calling at weird times of the night because of a woman, and you know who you are; it is work hours, we are working right now. It becomes an idol. The sister you are asking for may be physically attractive but spiritually may not be, and she has become an idol to you. And the same with you sisters: men become an idol.

precepts.why:
Just on that sports image on the screen, to show you that this is actually real: “Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest; That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple”. Some of our brothers in the world right now know what the truth is, but they cannot give it up, because they are so connected to that idol. They cannot leave the lifestyle. They cannot leave none of it.

Remember sports is actually a Greek fashion. Sports is a Greek fashion. That is why, when we went to Greece and Rome, a lot of the coliseums you see are shaped the same way as these football stadiums today — the seating, the layout, the bricks, the main floor, which would be the pitch, the turf. It is exactly the same. The coliseum we went to in Rome is one of the ones the slave trade funded; that is the bottom line, the slave trade funded that coliseum. We were standing right at the top of the amphitheatre, where the gladiators were. It was huge, that place — seats for at least a hundred thousand people minimum. And the gladiators: we were the ones. She tried to lie and say we did it willingly, that the black gladiators were willing volunteers to fight in the coliseum, and that they were wealthy as well, so they could roll in and roll out when they wanted, pull up, do their thing and have a big bag of money at the end of it — which is not true. It is something we were a part of.

So it got to a point where the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, meaning: you know what, to hell with this truth, to hell with the prophecies that are coming out, to hell with our salvation, I am going to go on and fulfil what is out there. And despising the temple means despising the ministry, despising the work. They forgot everything, they put everything to bed, all to follow the heathenish fashions. That is what it is today: it is a lifestyle. Some of you may have kids that are aspiring to do these things right now, and they have to see the vision of it — and guess what, all of that is going to come to naught at some point. What do they say today in this life to make it? Either you have got to be a musician or a sports entertainer: a boxer, a footballer, one of these things. If you are not any of those things, you are dead weight. And that is how some of our brothers in the world look at us today: are these guys in purple talking about keep the commandments? To hell with that, I am trying to do this, you are trying to be against my dream. No — you are idolizing. You forgot the Lord.

Remember the captivity before Rome was the Greek captivity, and under that there were four generals that ruled in different parts. And when we went to Ephesus, the same thing: when Paul went out he cried out in the amphitheatre and our people were crying out, praising her. These are the things that were happening. It is the same thing today: whatever captivity we are in, there is always an idol, and there is always a trend of something. The Olympics and all of that stems right back from the Greeks.

“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.” Because guess what, some of us are actually coming from those lifestyles. Some of us are coming from those idolatry lifestyles.

Whatever it was that was an idol prior to this truth, anything that you were doing prior to this truth — it might not have been football, it could have been something else, it could have been your so-called boyfriend, it could have been whatever — all of that is idolatry, because you put that before the Lord. Anything you put before the Lord is idolatry, because you idolize it, you put it first. But now we have got the spirit of remembrance, and he shall bring all things to your remembrance. We are coming back to our true heritage, knowing what we have to do to get the kingdom of God.

So now we have that understanding. We know who we are, keeping God's commandments. Some of us have been in the world and you know what a wicked time is, but we are done now; the Lord had mercy, we have come in, we are done now. Let us move forward from that and keep God's commandments. But a lot of us slide back into it and idolize all of that stuff. Some people envy one another. Blood toucheth blood: people killing one another to make sure they can succeed in this life, making this place their kingdom. That is why, brothers, we have to stay strong, stay focused, stay diligent, because it is a fight. We are warring for the hearts of our people, for their minds to change, for them to see what we see. We see the matrix. We see the end. So we have got to stay locked in.

sense.text:
“Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” Because if you have that idol of being on social media constantly, eventually you are going to want that lifestyle. And that is why a lot of these crimes happen.

They are on social media scrolling, looking at these footballers or these models or whatever these people do. They are seeing the chains, the women, the lifestyle, and they are saying, I want that lifestyle. So now they become corrupted by it, and they do anything by any means to get it. That is where you get the stabbings, the killings. Now they want that name. They want to be a name brand. They want their name to ring bells like rappers.

And the rappers glorify the drill music. All they talk about is killing: splash this, splash that, score a point here, score a point there. That is enticing them to want to do wickedness, so that they can say it themselves. They say, I spilled juice on my knife. Now they can say it, because they have heard it in the music; it has enticed their spirit, it has riled them up. Now these people that were not even bad before, that were not doing any of this wickedness before, have been corrupted to it. Now they want to join a gang, now they want to be part of that lifestyle, so they can sing the song and say they mean it, that they lived it.

That is why the Lord says it in Proverbs 1: “My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.” If sinners entice you — will it be by the things you see, or the words they speak unto you, the dream they sell to you? If sinners entice you, what does it say? Consent thou not. Do not consent to them.

“If they say, Come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause:” If they say, come with us, be like us. Remember the topic is blood toucheth blood. So these sinners might say to you, come with us, let us lay wait for blood.

Like that delivery driver. He is innocent. He is not part of any gang, he is not doing anything, he is trying to make some money for his family. But the man is robbing him with his knife.

And we have got a saying in London: we say let's lurk, we're lurking. It means you are looking for someone to do something to. Like the man who got punched up in the chicken shop — the one who did it would have said, I am lurking, trying to find someone like that, and he moved to him and beat him up. London lingo.

“Let us swallow them up alive as the grave; and whole, as those that go down into the pit: We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoil: Cast in thy lot among us; let us all have one purse:” They are looking to rob them, to become more rich by their gains.

“My son, walk not thou in the way with them; refrain thy foot from their path:” That is the message he is saying: do not walk in the way of them. Do not be enticed by this lifestyle. Do not be enticed by this. Do not glorify this. The world glorifies this. The music we listen to glorifies this — well, the music we should not be listening to. What they are promoting in the world now, in America and in the UK: the Chicago rap, the London drill.

But we are meant to refrain our way from this path. We have already read how blood toucheth blood. We had a history of killing each other and it is still happening today. That is why you need to listen when the prophets are teaching, telling you to come out of it. Do not follow this. You do not want to be the one on the internet, on Telegram, being an example of what we should not be doing.

“For their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed blood.” The Lord has got our people down to a tee. He said their feet run to evil. We run to it. We enjoy it. And it said make haste to shed blood: quick to draw a knife.

Like you saw with the machete, and the man in the cab when he is getting stabbed up in the cab. There are many different examples where you see how people are hasty to shed blood. We need to come out of it. That is what the law is trying to show you.

“And they lay wait for their own blood; they lurk privily for their own lives.” They lay wait for their own blood. It is always our own people we are looking to kill. It is always our own that is dying. And we are always trying to say stop black on black crime, black power — but we are killing each other. We need to stop it. We need to come back to the commandments of God.

“Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” So the Lord has made his words known unto us today, telling us to love each other as we love ourselves: to stop the killing, stop the shooting, stop the stabbings.

“Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded;” He is calling us. How? When you see the men teaching on the streets, when you watch the classes online — he is calling you, telling you to repent. But our people refuse.

What did the man say today when he was told to change? He said, I want to change, but I can't; I have got some ops that I want to deal with first. The Lord is telling you to change now. What do you mean you have got to deal with ops first? So you are going to wait till one of you dies, and then you say, okay Lord, I am ready now? It does not make any sense. That is how the cycle keeps going and going and going.
“But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof:” So we did not want to take the Lord's correction. And what is the Lord going to do?

“I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;” The Lord said he is going to laugh at your calamity. If we do not take heed to his warnings, if we do not learn from the history of our forefathers, if we do not learn from what we see today on TV, the Lord said he is going to laugh at our calamity. When the tables turn and come back on you, like Abimelech, he is going to laugh at you.

And he is going to mock when your fear cometh. When it is your turn now — because everyone is good when they have got the upper hand, but when the flip side comes and you are the one getting chased, because the Lord is judging your behind, he said he is going to mock you when your fear cometh.

“Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:” So then you want to call on God: God help me, God save me. The Lord already tried to save you. He told you to repent. The man was in the streets teaching. But now you are saying, God help me, in your hospital bed. God help me.

And what did the Lord say? But I will not answer. He said he is not going to answer. That is why we have got to change our ways.

“For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.” Why? Because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord.

So we cannot despise the Lord's correction. You should hear these words and think, the Lord has got us down packed to a tee. We need to fix this stuff and fix our community and come out of this wickedness.

But it all starts from the things we watch. If you are enticed by these things on social media — they put people getting stabbed on Instagram and stuff — we need to stop. We need to drop it out.

We are coming to the end now, so go back to Wisdom of Solomon 14 and verse 12 — “For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life.” — and then verse 27: “For the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil.”

So all of this we have brought out today all stems from, or revolves around, idolatry. Whether it is power — and for the most part we have been dealing with power — material goods, or financial gain: these are the things which have caused us to go off, these are the things which caused us to deal treacherously with each other.

As a community we need to put that to bed and stop doing it. That is why we are out on the streets teaching. That is what we do.
